name: Amorpha

project_scope.source_pool: Master Plant Pool; Genus Study Index
project_scope.scientific_status_boundary: Preserve canonical native_target_zone_calculated false for A. canescens and true for A. fruticosa and A. roemeriana; no county determinations here.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Pick apart one tiny flower in the purple terminal raceme: Amorpha has only ONE true petal (the banner/standard), not banner + two wings + two keel petals. Look for ten stamens fused near the base and projecting beyond the calyx. Then compare plant height, leaflet hairiness, leaflets and mature short pods.
shared_traits: Perennial woody shrubs or low subshrubs with alternate odd-pinnate leaves bearing numerous often gland-dotted leaflets.
Small purple/violet single-banner flowers densely packed into terminal spike-like racemes; ten stamens united basally with protruding filaments.
Small compressed, generally indehiscent one- or two-seeded legumes, often with glandular surface. Examine calyx and pod, not purple color.
shared_genus_recognition.where_to_look_tip: Use a magnifier on a fresh flower: one true standard petal, not a tiny ordinary five-petal pea flower.

species_comparison_matrix.A. canescens: Low rhizomatous prairie subshrub, often gray and 0.3–1 m
species_comparison_matrix.A. fruticosa: Tall robust shrub, often 2–3 m or more, common on streambanks
species_comparison_matrix.A. roemeriana: Upright deciduous woody shrub, usually smaller than A. fruticosa, often on limestone slopes
species_comparison_matrix.weight: FIRST FIELD SPLIT; habitat is supporting only

species_comparison_matrix.character: hair layer on leaflets and stems
species_comparison_matrix.A. canescens: Very dense gray-whitish silky/canescent hair covering much foliage
species_comparison_matrix.A. fruticosa: Green leaflets, variable sparse/downy hairs, often on lower veins; not overall densely silver-gray
species_comparison_matrix.A. roemeriana: Mostly green and glabrous or nearly so, lacking leadplant's gray felt

species_comparison_matrix.A. canescens: Many small leaflets, often 11–41 or more
species_comparison_matrix.A. fruticosa: Frequently ~9–21, sometimes more, broader/longer than leadplant
species_comparison_matrix.A. roemeriana: Numerous relatively broad, mostly smooth leaflets; overlap; photograph a complete leaf and count
species_comparison_matrix.weight: SUPPORTING; numerical overlap means no absolute key

species_comparison_matrix.A. canescens: Single banner petal; many narrow dense upright racemes often crowded into terminal compound cluster
species_comparison_matrix.A. fruticosa: Single banner petal; usually 1–4 longer terminal/upper-axillary racemes
species_comparison_matrix.A. roemeriana: Single banner petal; terminal violet racemes, compare bracts/calyx and flowers in macro
species_comparison_matrix.weight: GENUS LOCK; raceme clustering may assist

species_comparison_matrix.A. canescens: Very small 1-seeded pod generally enclosed by or near persistent calyx; confirm texture with macro
species_comparison_matrix.A. fruticosa: Larger gland-dotted or warty compressed pod, commonly 1–2 seeds
species_comparison_matrix.A. roemeriana: Short compressed pods; mature pod and calyx measurement needed for rigorous separation from fruticosa
species_comparison_matrix.weight: REPRODUCTIVE VALIDATION; no unverified hard thresholds

species_comparison_matrix.A. fruticosa: Streambanks, riparian thickets and wetter edges
species_comparison_matrix.A. roemeriana: Rocky limestone slopes and oak/juniper woodland openings
species_comparison_matrix.weight: CONTEXT ONLY; never native range proof

look_here_first_sequence.if: one violet banner but no wings or keel, plus ten protruding partially united stamens
look_here_first_sequence.then: Amorpha likely; verify gland-dotted pinnate leaflets and small legume

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: whole plant and close-ups of both leaflet surfaces
look_here_first_sequence.if: small prairie subshrub with uniformly dense gray/white pubescence
look_here_first_sequence.then: A. canescens leadplant candidate; preserve its unresolved/fail target-zone native label as in canonical record

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: green-leaved woody shrub; stem base, complete pinnate leaf and racemes
look_here_first_sequence.if: tall robust riparian shrub with relatively large leaflets and 1–4 long racemes
look_here_first_sequence.then: A. fruticosa candidate; inspect pods and lower leaf hair

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: green woody shrub from limestone slopes, with magnified leaflets and fruit
look_here_first_sequence.if: smaller smooth-leaved shrub with terminal racemes
look_here_first_sequence.then: A. roemeriana candidate; do not force when fruticosa characters overlap
Record Amorpha sp. until full flowering/fruit and vegetative macro set

scientific_cautions: A. fruticosa and A. roemeriana can overlap in size and leaflet pubescence; mature calyx/pod structure and authoritative regional keys remain a scientific-review dependency for difficult observations.
A. canescens retains its prior project range determination (not confirmed target-zone native); this genus lesson does not turn occurrence in Texas into local confirmation.
Amorpha has only the banner petal; calling its flowers normal five-petaled pea flowers would misteach the genus.
Multiple racemes create a clustered display, not a grass spike; inspect individual flowers and axillary/terminal peduncles.
Purple flowers, dry versus riparian site, and number of leaflets alone are not reliable species identifications.
A. roemeriana synonyms in the species.json include Amorpha texana and Amorpha subglabra; route these to the established concept rather than new species.

local_lookalike_routing.separator: Often also violet, crowded inflorescences but flowers have a modified multi-petaled papilionoid plan; dissect corolla and inspect pod and floral bracts.
Also compound-leaved woody Fabaceae, but flowers have five pale petals rather than the single Amorpha banner; confirm floral anatomy.
Require standard + wings + keel in ordinary pea-like flowers; only the banner in Amorpha.
Bipinnate leaves and showy many-stamen puffballs; not the Amorpha odd-pinnate leaf plus single-banner raceme.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: isolated solitary banner, empty wing/keel positions, 10 basally united stamens, staminal tube and calyx; millimeter ruler

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: matched leaflet upper/lower surface hair macro
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: dense gray silk vs sparse vein hairs vs glabrous leaflet; same magnification and lighting

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: complete leaf on branch plus scale
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: odd pinnation, count leaflets, leaflet length, translucent gland dots when possible
low grassland subshrub vs robust tall riparian shrub vs Hill Country limestone shrub; don't imply habitat is a hard diagnostic
pod size, shape, gland-dots, calyx lobes, seeds; add same-scale measurement to test fruticosa/roemeriana overlap
terminal racemes and number/clustering, with flower dissection as genus confirmation

handoffs.question: Find and verify reproducible calyx-lobe and mature pod dimensions/gland characters from an authoritative regional key; do not publish an unsupported numerical boundary.
Match lower leaflet hair macros, flowers proving the single-petal condition, and mature pods at identical scales; source rights/attribution mandatory.
Three species already canonical; no installation changes needed and no reclassification of A. canescens nativity.
